From a standard DCGAN to my GAN

My first try was a plain DCGAN. Here is what I changed, and why.

GAN
Standard DCGANMy GANWhy
Forger
No label: draws a random imageThe letter steers every layer (conditional batch norm)To draw the letter I ask for
Noise enters once, at the inputNoise split into 6 slices, one per block (skip-z)So the Forger can't ignore the noise
Transposed convolutionsNearest upsample, then 3×3 convolutionNo checkerboard marks
Plain conv stack, 64 × 64Residual blocks, 128 × 128Smoother strokes at higher resolution
Detector
Batch normSpectral normalisation on every layerStops it overpowering the Forger
LeakyReLU (0.2)ReLUSpectral norm keeps gradients alive
Sigmoid + cross-entropy lossRaw score + hinge lossA sigmoid saturates, starving the Forger
One realness outputProjection head: real? and this letter?Checks the letter, not just the style
Training
No augmentationDiffAugment: random shift + cutoutOnly 3,714 letters: stops memorising
Nothing against mode collapseMode-seeking lossDifferent noise, different letters
One learning rate, 0.0002Detector 0.0004, Forger 0.0001 (TTUR)Keeps the Detector a useful teacher
Samples from the latest weightsEMA: an averaged copy of the ForgerSmoother final letters

Conditional batch norm, up close

How one Forger draws 12 different letters

GAN
Plain batch norm
Normalises each channel over the batch, then applies one learned scale γ and shift β. They are the same for every image, so the layer can't know which letter to draw.
x̂ = (x − μ) / σ,   then  y = γ·x̂ + β
Conditional batch norm (CondBN)
γ and β are no longer fixed. Two small linear layers compute them from the condition: the letter's 128-number embedding plus this block's 20-number slice of z (148 numbers). So every channel in every block gets a letter-specific scale and shift.
y = x̂ · (1 + γ(c)) + β(c)
class CondBN(nn.Module): # from my notebook, shortened
self.bn = nn.BatchNorm2d(ch, affine=False)
self.gain = nn.Linear(cond_dim, ch) # gives γ(c)
self.bias = nn.Linear(cond_dim, ch) # gives β(c)
return self.bn(x) * (1 + self.gain(c)) + self.bias(c)
# used twice in each of the 5 Forger blocks
Real scales 1 + γ(c) from my Forger
block 1, first 24 of its 512 channels, same z, two letters
letter அ letter இdashed line: scale 1 = unchanged
Same z, only the letter changes
The noise keeps the handwriting style; CondBN switches the letter.

One block (DResBlock)
ReLU → 3×3 conv → ReLU → 3×3 conv → 2×2 average pool, plus a 1×1 shortcut. Each block halves the size.
Spectral normalisation
Every weight is divided by its largest singular value, so no layer stretches its input more than ×1. Scores stay smooth, so the Forger always gets a useful gradient.
Projection head
No sigmoid: the raw score goes to the hinge loss. 9.61 M parameters.

Spectral normalisation, up close

Why my Detector can't overpower my Forger

GAN
The problem it solves
In my first run the Detector got too strong: its loss fell to about 0.2 while the Forger's loss jumped from 2 to 10. Its scores became a cliff, and a cliff gives the Forger no useful slope to climb.
The fix: limit how sharply each Detector layer can react.
What it does
Every weight matrix W stretches some input directions more than others. The biggest stretch is its spectral norm σ(W), the largest singular value. Spectral normalisation divides W by it, so no layer can stretch its input by more than ×1.
W_SN = W / σ(W)
# σ(W) is estimated with 1 power-iteration step per update:
# u ← Wv / ‖Wv‖, v ← Wᵀu / ‖Wᵀu‖, σ ≈ uᵀWv (no full SVD)
SN = nn.utils.parametrizations.spectral_norm
self.c1 = sn(nn.Conv2d(cin, cout, 3, 1, 1)) # every conv
self.proj = sn(nn.Embedding(n_cls, 512)) # and the head
What σ means

ReLU, LeakyReLU and Tanh: why and where

Activation functions decide what each neuron passes on, and where I used each one

GAN
ReLUmax(0, x)
Used in
every Forger blockevery Detector blockYuNet, every DWUnit
Why: Fast, and for positive inputs the gradient is 1, so deep networks keep learning.
Weak spot: a neuron stuck below 0 passes no gradient. My Detector can use plain ReLU because spectral norm keeps its gradients smooth.
LeakyReLUx if x > 0, else a·x
Used in
classic DCGAN Discriminator (a = 0.2)my ARCH = "dcgan" option (a = 0.1)
Why: Negatives still pass a little, so the gradient never dies.
The Forger learns only through the Detector's gradient. Without spectral norm, dead ReLUs could block it.
Tanhsqueezes x into −1 … +1
Used in
Forger, last layer only
Why: Pixels come out between −1 (paper) and +1 (ink), exactly how the real letters were scaled.
Bounded and smooth, so strokes can't blow up.
No sigmoid in my Detectorhinge loss uses the raw score. YuNet does use a sigmoid for its face scores.

Training: a two-step dance

Every step, the networks take turns. The other one stays frozen.

GAN
Step 1: train the Detector
Forger frozen
score ≥ +1
score ≤ −1
DiffAugment: same random shift + cutout on both
LD = E[max(0, 1 − D(x,y))] + E[max(0, 1 + D(G(z,y),y))]
Adam, learning rate 0.0004
Step 2: train the Forger
Detector frozen
push score up
mode-seeking: two z, same letter → must look different
LG = −E[D(G(z,y),y)] + λ / min(div, target)
Adam, learning rate 0.0001
10,000 steps, batch 64TTUR: Detector learns 4× fasterEMA: an averaged Forger draws the final letters49.5 min on a Colab T4

Mode collapse, and how I fixed it

When the Forger stops being creative

GAN
What it is
The Forger finds a few shapes that fool the Detector and draws only those. Different noise z gives the same letter: each one may look fine, but the variety of handwriting is gone. It is one of the most common ways GAN training fails, and plain DCGAN has nothing against it.
What collapse looks like (illustration)
z1
z2
z3
z4
4 different z,
1 drawing
Why it happens
The Forger is rewarded only for fooling the Detector, never for variety. If one shape works, repeating it is the easiest win. In a DCGAN the noise enters only at the input, so the Forger can learn to ignore it.
Fix 1: skip-z
My 120 noise numbers are split into 6 slices of 20. Each Forger block gets its own slice through CondBN, so the noise reaches every layer and can't be ignored.
z → [z1 | z2 | z3 | z4 | z5 | z6]
Fix 2: mode-seeking loss
Two different z for the same letter must give different images. If they look alike, div is small and the penalty is big.
div = mean|G(z1)−G(z2)| / mean|z1−z2|
L_G = −D(G(z)) + λ / min(div, target)
λ = 1, target = 0.9 × the variety of real handwriting
Result: 6 different z, letter அ
six different handwritings from my trained Forger

How I measured accuracy
1
Train a judge on real letters only: ResNet-18 recogniser, 3,714 real training letters. It reads 98.3% of the real test letters correctly.
2
Forge 2,476 letters: the same number as the test set, spread evenly over the 12 letters
3
The judge reads every forgery: it has never seen a forged letter
4
Forgery accuracy: the share it reads as the letter I asked for
Why a judge? A GAN has no right answer to compare with, so a model that reads real handwriting well acts as the examiner.
91.6%of forgeries read as the intended letter
per letter; pink = under 80% (the loopy இ 69.1% and அ 76.8%)

How YuNet was trained

PyTorch and MMDetection, from scratch, on WIDER FACE

YuNet
1. Data
WIDER FACE: 32,203 images, 393,703 faces
easymediumhard
2. Augment
random square crop, scale 0.5 to 1.5, resized to 640 × 640

flip left-right, 50%
This range keeps face sizes closest to the real data, which gave the best average AP (0.862).
3. Match
Each real face is assigned to the cells whose guesses fit it best (simOTA). Those cells must learn that face.
4. Loss: four parts, weighted
face or not
×1cross-entropy, IoU as soft label
object or not
×1cross-entropy
box
×5EIoU loss
5 landmarks
×0.1Smooth L1
5. Optimiser: SGD
momentum 0.9weight decay 0.0005 batch 16 × 2 GPUswarm-up 1,500 iterationsno pretraining
